statement: Let n = len(groupSizes). Whenever the function returns a result r (i.e. Ok r), the following hold: (a) for every index a with 0 <= a < len(r), len(r[a]) >= 1; (b) for every index a and j with 0 <= a < len(r) and 0 <= j < len(r[a]), 0 <= r[a][j] < n and len(r[a]) = groupSizes[r[a][j]]; (c) for every person i with 0 <= i < n, the number of pairs (a,j) with 0 <= a < len(r), 0 <= j < len(r[a]), and r[a][j] = i is exactly 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(groupSizes). 1 <= n <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= groupSizes[i] <= n; and for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n, if C_k is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and groupSizes[i] = k, then C_k is a multiple of k.
